open_items.finding: Running three sub-agents concurrently inside ONE product worktree materially degrades source-provenance-bound proofs. Several MTs (notably MT-027, MT-066, MT-068) bind their official proof to an exact committed HEAD, but while other agents hold uncommitted edits no agent can bind a clean tree. Observed concretely: the MT-029 run5 compiled input is NOT byte-identical to HEAD b0d84cfc because the tree simultaneously held MT-079 uncommitted app.rs edits and MT-111 uncommitted event_emitter.rs edits. The MT-029 agent handled this correctly and honestly - it recorded the exact dirty set to mt029_run5_source_state.txt and will report the matrix as bound to HEAD PLUS a named delta rather than falsely claiming a clean-HEAD binding.
secondary_symptoms: Agents repeatedly block on the SHARED ~/.cargo package-cache lock, which scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR does not isolate; observed blocking three cargo invocations at once.

Agents have had to commit each other in-flight work (5968bb36, 110389fd, fcf49702) purely so a source-bound gate could bind a clean HEAD - work is preserved, but authorship attribution in the history becomes muddled.
One agent mid-edit file broke another agent build for roughly 15 minutes.

KERNEL_BUILDER committed the tree once (5dc08b0f) to give the gated MTs a clean HEAD.
open_items.recommended_fix: For the REMAINING source-provenance-bound MTs, SERIALIZE: run at most one agent whose proof binds an exact committed HEAD, and let concurrent agents work only on MTs whose proofs are not source-bound. The alternative - one worktree per concurrent MT - is forbidden here because KERNEL_BUILDER_PROTOCOL restricts worktree creation to the WP activation phase and the WP worktree budget is 1 per WP.

kernel_builder_root_cause.mechanism: The test stands up its OWN deterministic 404 server on an EPHEMERAL port (it reads listener.local_addr(), so a fixed-port collision is ruled out - that was the obvious hypothesis and it is wrong). The server thread runs a hard 10-SECOND deadline and panics with "memory-pack 404 was not requested" if the shell has not issued the memory-pack read by then. That is the unnamed-thread panic seen at test_app_host_mount_secondary.rs:3540 in the full-binary run.
kernel_builder_root_cause.why_it_fails_only_in_the_full_binary: cargo runs the binary 51 tests in PARALLEL by default. Under that load the shell does not reach its FEMS refresh-for-context within the fixed 10s window, the server thread dies on its deadline, and the downstream assertion ever_in_flight (AC-080-5) then fails. Run alone, the read fires immediately - observed printing "relevant_memory: ever_requested=true got_blocker=true" and passing 1/0.
kernel_builder_root_cause.classification: TEST ROBUSTNESS under parallelism, NOT a product defect and NOT MT-113 fallout. The product behaviour it asserts (the shell drives the FEMS read, and a 404 surfaces as a typed blocker) is demonstrably correct when given time.
kernel_builder_root_cause.how_to_fix_without_weakening_anything: Do NOT relax the ASSERTIONS - ever_in_flight and the typed blocker are the real contract and must stay. The 10s wall-clock deadline is the fragile part. Prefer making the wait condition-based with a generous bound, or serialising this test, over simply enlarging the constant. Note MT-113 hit a sibling of this class and solved it properly with an explicit quiescence gate rather than a longer sleep - the same instinct applies here.
kernel_builder_root_cause.impact_on_the_capstone: MT-108 item 11 requires the full suite to pass. A test that is green alone and red in its own binary makes that sweep NON-DETERMINISTIC, so this must be fixed before the capstone rather than discovered inside it. Recording it now is the difference between a known 10-minute fix and an unexplained capstone failure.

RESOLVED.fix: Widened the server ANTI-HANG GUARD from 10s to 120s in tests/test_app_host_mount_secondary.rs, with the reasoning documented at the site.
RESOLVED.precise_root_cause: The two bounds were mismatched in KIND: the client loop is ITERATION-bounded (80 x run_steps(2) plus a 25ms sleep) while the server guard was TIME-bounded at 10s. Under cargo default 51-way parallelism the client fixed iterations outlast a 10s clock, the server thread panics, and server.join() converts that into a failure of an otherwise-correct test.
RESOLVED.hypothesis_checked_and_rejected: A fixed-port collision between parallel tests was the obvious explanation and is WRONG - the server binds an EPHEMERAL port via listener.local_addr(). Verified in source before changing anything.
RESOLVED.nothing_weakened: No assertion was relaxed. ever_in_flight (AC-080-5) and the typed blocker remain exactly as written, and the widened guard CANNOT mask a defect: if the shell never issues the read, the client loop still completes and ever_in_flight still fails.

finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.owner: UNASSIGNED - repo tooling, outside every current microtask scope
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.finding: Two places default cargo builds into ONE shared, unscoped target directory, so any two lanes running at once contend on a single cargo file lock. (1) .cargo/config.toml at the repo root sets target-dir = "../Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target", which every build inherits unless it explicitly overrides CARGO_TARGET_DIR. (2) The governed MT auto-relay hook, .GOV/roles_shared/scripts/hooks/post-commit-mt-review-request.mjs, hardcodes the same path at line 128 and runs cargo check inline at line 121 on any commit with a feat: MT-NNN subject.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.precision_correction: The implementing agent reported this as landing in "the directory CX-984-002 forbids". That overstates it and a validator would chase the wrong thing. Verified: the path resolves to Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target, which IS the permitted artifacts root. The defect is that it is SHARED and unscoped, not that it is forbidden. The genuinely forbidden siblings are Handshake/Handshake_Artifacts and Handshake Worktrees/handshake-cargo-target, and neither is in play here.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.why_it_matters: The hook is the sharper half. It runs a compile gate inline on the shared target dir, so a concurrent lane holding that lock can starve it into the TIMEOUT_INCONCLUSIVE branch at line 150 - which tells the validator to treat compile evidence as inconclusive. The governed auto-relay can therefore be made to emit a degraded verdict by unrelated work simply running at the same time. That is a governance-tooling defect, not a product one.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.observed_this_session: Three lanes ran concurrently. Every one had to be given an owner-scoped CARGO_TARGET_DIR by hand to avoid contending, and the operator had to be told explicitly why. The MT-146 lane also deliberately sequenced its product build after its suite for exactly this reason, and one false negative was already attributed to this class of starvation.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.suggested_scope: Decide whether the default should be owner-scoped (per worktree or per lane) rather than shared, and make the hook use a scoped dir or skip its inline compile gate when the lock is held rather than timing out into an inconclusive verdict.
finding_2026_09_05_shared_cargo_target.evidence: Verified by the orchestrator: cat .cargo/config.toml resolving to Handshake Worktrees/Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-cargo-target; and grep of post-commit-mt-review-request.mjs showing the cargo check at line 121, the hardcoded CARGO_TARGET_DIR at line 128, and the TIMEOUT_INCONCLUSIVE branch at line 150.

finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.owner: UNASSIGNED - test harness; related to but distinct from the MT-123 teardown defect
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.finding: The in-crate api::memory:: suite livelocks at DEFAULT libtest parallelism when the host is carrying other cargo work. Measured: 29 tests launched simultaneously at 23:45:39, each opening its own embedded RocksDB store, 26 store directories created in one burst and none afterwards. After 3.8 hours only 4 of 29 tests had completed and 25 were sitting in the has-been-running-for-over-60-seconds state.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.why_it_is_not_simply_the_teardown_drain: An earlier run of this same suite completed in 2255 seconds at the same parallelism with the same 30-second teardown drain per store. The drain alone therefore does not explain it. The variable is host contention: with nine cargo and rustc processes resident from other lanes, 26-way concurrent store access turns ordinary contention into a livelock rather than a slowdown.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.how_it_disguises_itself: Every outward signal says healthy. The process is alive, CPU is non-zero and advancing, and no error is emitted. Two things give it away, and neither is visible without deliberately looking: no new store directory is created after the initial burst, and the working set collapses (2.6 GB down to 0.3 GB) as the tests stop doing work. Log output is also block-buffered when redirected, so the log itself looks frozen and gives no help either way.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.orchestrator_error_worth_recording: I initially accepted a non-zero CPU delta as proof the run was progressing, and agreed to let it continue on that basis. Advancing and making progress through the suite are different claims and I let the first stand in for the second, which cost additional waiting. The store-directory count is the signal that actually distinguishes them.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.mitigation_that_works: Cap libtest concurrency. The MT-145 lane ran both its suites at --test-threads=4 under the same host load and completed. The MT-146 lane relaunched at 4 after the stall. Serial (--test-threads=1) is not the answer either: the fixed teardown cost alone would put this suite near two hours.
finding_2026_09_05_suite_livelock.suggested_scope: Decide whether these suites should carry a default thread cap in configuration rather than relying on every operator to pass it, and whether the embedded store harness should bound concurrent stores directly. Pairs naturally with the MT-123 teardown work and with the shared cargo target dir finding, since all three are about concurrent lanes interfering.
